mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.2% in a month coincides with a 20-day positive S&P 500 forward return, reflecting market anticipation of rate cuts by the Federal Reserve.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.2% in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month rolling window, 20-day forward returns do not outperform a 5-day moving average baseline during inflation spikes above 0.2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly PAYEMS rises by more than 2,000 in a single month, it indicates strengthening labor market conditions and supports higher consumer confidence, which drives a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Across 10 such labor strength events, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during comparable periods of muted labor data (Mann-Whitney U p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both HOUST (housing starts) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 5% in the same month predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak demand signals contraction in economic activity.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < prev_month by ≥5% AND RSAFS < prev_month by ≥5%
failure_condition: During 10 such dual declines, the 20-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant mean negative deviation from a control group (bootstrap p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in INDPRO below 100 (indexing to 2017=100) followed by a subsequent month's recovery above 101 indicates a supply-side shock, which is associated with a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Over 8 such episodes, the 5-day forward returns are not consistently negative (mean p-value across episodes > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25 percentage points in a month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return tends to be negative, reflecting market anticipation of tighter policy and reduced growth expectations.
failure_condition: During 12 such tightening months, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during comparable pre-tightening months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month declining trend in UNRATE predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as lower expected wage growth reduces labor cost pressures and boosts equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE is in a downward trend for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 7 such downward-trend episodes, the 60-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant positive deviation from a neutral baseline (bootstrap p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly drop in GDPC1 (consumer demand) of at least 3% and a rise in HOUST by at least 4% suggests conflicting signals but overall weak demand, resulting in a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < prev_month by ≥3% AND HOUST > prev_month by ≥4%
failure_condition: During 6 such events, the 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative (mean p-value > 0.10 across tests).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of GDPC1 exceeds its 12-month moving average by at least 5%, it indicates a structural shift toward stronger demand, which is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return in expansionary regimes.
candidate_trigger: 3-month GDPC1 MA exceeds 12-month GDPC1 MA by ≥5%
failure_condition: During 8 such structural shifts in expansion regimes, the 60-day forward returns do not outperform a neutral benchmark (median p-value > 0.10).
